title: On tour with Victoria Spivey's revue and the Tulsa hotel
summary: Tate toured with the Spivey revue, who had made the film Hallelujah, and describes the Tulsa hotel with a lobby piano where musicians jammed.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Then when I hear him again maybe three years later, Pres was with him, he was playing tenor with him. So I was with Victoria Spivey, she had a review, she had two million-dollar sellers, records, and she was in the first black picture that was produced by a big white production, you know, like King Vidor, and the picture was "Hallelujah" and it was ----- a pretty girl by the name of Nina Mae McKinney then, you know, she was in the picture and so was Victoria Spivey in the picture. So after she made the picture, she came to Dallas and got this revue, beautiful girls, and we were on a tour and we went to Tulsa, Oklahoma. Now we stayed at a hotel in Tulsa, Oklahoma. The name of the hotel -- it was a small hotel -- that was the best hotel in the world for blacks. He was an oil magnate and we stayed in there. And in the lobby, had a big baby grand in the lobby, and musicians would come in and jam. You know, they'd come in, this one would play hour, a half hour, and they always had some nice music in there.
